items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: I think, I don't know if it was Emile Christian's brother or Emile himself had a band. Christian band.

ctx.x: Anything else you remember around in there or later on? Later on? Yeah, they had a lot of things happen. Well, you see a millen boy. Gee, that was New Orleans. New Orleans was New Orleans at that time. You see, modern times, I mean, it changed everything. They had a lot of camps. Just like they have now in some parts of Littlewood. You know, out on the lake, the camp's out on the lake. Well, that's... It was flooded out there with camps. And people had picnics every day. Every day. And when they had a picnic,…
The straight line on the bandstand, yeah. Well, you had the bass, then they had the guitar, the clarinet, the clarinet player, the trombone

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: I remember a band called, I just mentioned his dance, well, Emil Christian, man. The Christian band.

ctx.x: No, I didn't sit in there. I mean, the guys would be bucking one another, you know what I mean about it, blowing at each other, you know. And sometimes we'd have 10 bands, maybe 15 bands playing all at the same time. You ever use a code of music and you know what was happening? Well, the people that was dancing to the music wouldn't know, you know, right then and there, you know. Right on that spot, you know, particular spot. They wouldn't know unless we'd stop playing or somebody else would stop playing. And the…
There were several of them, there's Charlie and Frank, too.
